The page documents the CV drift as a one-way trend; the Wellington consultation is the first reversal signal at a major council. Other NZ councils: not on the wiki beyond the Auckland 2010 amalgamation.
uncertainties: 'Preferred option' provenance: the queue says LV is 'the committee's preferred option'. That is documented only for the 25 June 2026 resolution ('Option 2 [preferred]', 16:2); the adopted 1 Oct consultation document and hub present LV as an open question ('whether to change') and stress 'no decision'. Say 'the committee identified consulting on a move to land value as its preferred option in June 2026; consultation opened 19 October' rather than 'proposes to adopt'. The commercial 3.0:1 option is labelled 'preferred' / 'Council's preferred option' in the 1 Oct amendment 2.17 and Table 1.

The queue item says the vacant-land differential is 'already 5x the base general rate in the central city'. The hub says 'five times'; the consultation document says '5.0 times'. Property Council material surfaced by web search mentions 5.1:1 in the 2024 LTP proposal; the Council's own current figure is 5.0. Use 5.0 / 'five times' from the Council documents.

Distributional figures at suburb level: the 25 June minutes contain extensive suburb tables (e.g. Kelburn, Churton Park) but these appear to be affordability (rates as % of income) tables from the Infometrics deck, not LV-vs-CV effects; none was used. No median-bill LV-vs-CV figure exists in the saved texts; the only per-property LV figures are the seven hypothetical-street examples (image) and the $1.5m commercial/residential figures for the differential change (which are CV-based).

The p.14 worked-example figures were transcribed by eye from a rendered image (220 dpi crop); T1 should confirm digits against the PDF page. Officers' prose in the June report confirms the direction for apartment/mixed-use/duplex/industrial but gives no dollar amounts.

Share of NZ councils rating on land value: the two sources give different series (Wellington: 65% CV in 2026, 58% in 2016, 50% in 2006, 51 of 78 councils; officers' Q&A text '35% use LV'; wiki's existing figure 29% LV / 71% CV in 2019 from the Productivity Commission analysis). The 2016 figure of 58% CV conflicts with 2019's 71%; probably different denominators (all councils vs territorial authorities; share of rateable properties vs councils). Do not merge.

Legal basis: only the Council's own statement that general rates are set under s.13 of the Local Government (Rating) Act 2002 and that the review proceeds under that Act and the LGA (ss.76-82, 101(3), 102) was captured. The text of s.13 (council may choose capital, land or annual value for a general rate) and the Rating Valuations Act 1998 were not fetched; do not attribute the statutory wording until retrieved. The existing wiki page already says LV rating is 'possible under current law except for Auckland Council' (citing the Productivity Commission), which is an adequate secondary basis.

Other NZ councils moving: only the Council's own slide lists HCC (Hutt City), PNCC (Palmerston North) and TCDC (Thames-Coromandel) as recent LV-to-CV switches; no council is documented moving CV-to-LV in the saved texts. A web-search snippet (not saved, not verified) says Thames-Coromandel decided in June 2025 to move LV to CV from 1 July 2026 and Central Otago was consulting on LV to CV from 1 July 2027; treat as a lead requiring retrieval before use.

The hub says 'Oral hearings: November'; no date or location was found. The December decision meeting is unspecified (CPF meets 10 Dec 2026 per the calendar; Council 17 Dec). The LTP formal consultation window is given as 'March and April 2027' in the resolution and 'April' in the news release.
Amalgamation of Wellington-region councils is an explicit risk to the timeline (Q&A 8-9, 18-21); regional reform could change the LV question; the page should state the outcome is open.

Common Ground Aotearoa (advocacy body, a public participant) is named in the 25 June minutes' conflict-of-interest note as a proponent of LV; Tier 2, origin/proponent only. Nine councillors recorded a campaign donation from an individual associated with it. This is a Council record but is not needed for the wiki and risks implying motive; recommend omitting the donation detail.
Property Council New Zealand also addressed the committee on 25 June (no content captured); it is a lobbying body (Tier 2) and has publicly argued for cutting the commercial differential; not saved.

wellington.govt.nz news release of 1 Oct 2026 says the consultation materials were approved 'by Te Taurapa'; the Council uses the te reo name with English 'Council Planning and Finance Committee'; use 'Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee' on first mention.
